newsitem.title: USA: U.S. meat companies cut beef, pork production.
newsitem.headline: U.S. meat companies cut beef, pork production.

text.p: IBP Inc said it reduced pork production at five of its seven pork plants this week, and about half of its pork plants will operate at reduced capacity next week because of poor operating margins.
Also, IBP and ConAgra announced cutbacks in beef production Thursday, which followed an Excel Corp announcement Tuesday of similar cutbacks. Excel is a division of Cargill Corp.
"Higher hog prices coupled with the lackluster movement of finished product have created margin problems," said Gary Mickelson, an IBP spokesman.
Next week about half of IBP's beef and pork plants will operate at 36 hours or less, with the balance running "no more than 40 hours," versus a normal 48-hour week, he said.
IBP this week cut beef plant operations to 40 hours or less per week from 48 at all but one of its beef carcass plants because of poor operating margins, Mickelson said.
ConAgra spokeswoman K.T. Miller said the company will cut beef production next week "and will continue to do so until demand and cattle supplies work out."
Excel said Tuesday it began reducing operations at its six beef plants this week because of tight cattle supply and negative packer margins.
ConAgra and Excel officials were unavailable to comment on whether there would be cutbacks at their hog plants.
